samples.question: The picture is a cream board scattered with small decorative squares that mean nothing. Somewhere on the board lies exactly one thin slate-grey THREAD: a single narrow line that runs as a staircase of short straight horizontal and vertical runs. It never crosses or touches itself, and one of its two ends is a thickened square CAP while the other end is plain. Sitting on the thread, each one straddling the thread so that the thread continues out of both of its sides, are several small square MARKS: most are coloured red, orange, yellow, green, blue or purple, and exactly one mark on the thread is BLACK. That black mark is the GATE. Only marks that sit on the thread count; every square that lies on the bare board away from the thread is decoration and means nothing, including decorative black and slate-grey squares. Walk along the thread starting at the thickened cap and meet the marks in the order in which you reach them, following every corner of the thread. Let k be the number of coloured marks you meet before you reach the black gate. Then carry on past the gate and count coloured marks again from the gate onwards: the answer is the k-th coloured mark after the gate. So the count taken on one stretch of the thread selects a position on the other stretch. The thread doubles back on itself, so the order along the thread is not the order of the marks by row, by column, or by straight-line distance from the cap, and each of those three sorts gives a different and wrong answer. k is always at least 2, so the answer is never the first coloured mark after the gate; the answer is never the last coloured mark on the thread, never the first coloured mark from the cap, and never the coloured mark just before the gate. The answer colour is always worn by at least two marks on the thread and is never the single commonest colour, so no colour, position, size, count or amount of ink identifies it on its own. Find that k-th coloured mark after the gate. What is its colour? Answer red, orange, yellow, green, blue or purple.
